newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CEZ SHARES TUMBLE IN TECHNICAL CORRECTION.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CEZ SHARES TUMBLE IN TECHNICAL CORRECTION.

text.p: Shares in Czech power utility CEZ tumbled during continuous trading on the Prague bourse on Friday but dealers said the fall was mainly due to a technical correction affecting most major issues.

At mid-session during continuous trading CEZ was down 47 crowns, 4.6 percent, to 961. "The reason for the fall is possibly just technical. Domestic and foreign investors are selling together," said Lubomir Vystavel of ING Barings.

Vystavel said the market was reacting to an accumulation of bad news about the Czech capital markets which are widely criticised for their lack of transparency and inadequate protection for minority shareholders.
He also said investors were reducing their exposure ahead of Senate elections scheduled for mid-November.
"There are just too many negative things and all this is making the major issues less interesting," he said.

Vystavel said CEZ's decline had little to do with a finance ministry decision on Thursday setting the company's 1996 supply prices to regional distributors retroactively at an average of 0.2 percent above those for 1995.
CEZ has long underperformed other major issues partly because electricity prices are strictly controlled by the finance ministry.
